name: Miami
tagline: Beach Life, Latin Culture, and Zero State Income Tax
description: Miami is a sun-drenched, cosmopolitan city where Latin American flair meets American ambition on the shores of Biscayne Bay. With no state income tax, year-round tropical weather, and one of the most dynamic food scenes in the country, Miami offers FIRE retirees a genuinely international lifestyle without leaving the United States. Housing costs are high and rising fast, especially in waterfront neighborhoods, but the trade-off is direct access to world-class beaches, a thriving arts district in Wynwood, and a multicultural energy that makes every day feel like a vacation.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.climate: Tropical with hot, humid summers and warm, dry winters

housing.description: Older studio/efficiency in Hialeah, Kendall, or outer Little Havana (citywide studio ~$1,828; Little Havana ~$1,779; frugal end ~$1,600)

dining.description: Cuban ventanitas and food trucks; mostly home cooking

healthcare.description: MAGI-managed subsidized ACA Silver/Bronze on the FL marketplace, kept under the 2026 400%-FPL cliff (~$62,600 single); income-capped contribution (~9.96% of MAGI). Above the cliff, premium tax credits vanish and this climbs to full price. Assumes an early retiree (45–55); older retirees budget more

transportation.description: Paid-off used car with Miami full coverage (~$389–408/mo, highest-premium FL metro) + gas + upkeep; a car is essential

entertainment.description: Free beaches (South Beach, Key Biscayne), Wynwood, public parks

1M.lifestyle: An older studio or efficiency in Hialeah, Kendall, or outer Little Havana anchors a frugal but genuinely livable stretch of Miami retirement, well away from the beach and Brickell. Housing and the two stubborn US floors — a subsidized ACA health premium held down by managing income under the returned 400%-FPL cliff, and a paid-off car carrying Miami's punishing auto-insurance rates — take most of the budget, so meals lean on home cooking with Cuban ventanitas as the treat. The beaches at South Beach and Key Biscayne, Wynwood's street art, and the public parks cost nothing, which is the whole point at this level. Florida's zero state income tax means every dollar of the drawdown stays in hand. It is disciplined living, but the setting never feels austere.

housing.description: Modest-to-nice 1BR in Edgewater, Midtown, or a newer Kendall building

dining.description: Regular dining in Wynwood and Brickell 3-4x/week; weekend brunch at waterfront cafes

healthcare.description: Full-price (unsubsidized) lowest-cost Silver/Bronze, ~48–50yo Miami-Dade — income now above the returned ACA cliff (the 500→850 jump IS the cliff)

transportation.description: Newer used car + premium Miami full coverage

entertainment.description: Heat games occasionally, Perez Art Museum, gym membership, salsa nights in Little Havana

2M.lifestyle: A comfortable one-bedroom in Edgewater, Midtown, or a newer Kendall building steps up into a real Miami neighborhood with the bay and nightlife close by. Income has crossed the ACA subsidy cliff at this level, so healthcare shifts to a full-price plan — a noticeable jump from the subsidized floor below — while a reliable car with full Miami coverage handles a spread-out city. Dining out several times a week across Wynwood and Brickell, a gym membership, and weekend trips to the Keys fit the budget. Zero state income tax keeps the whole withdrawal available to spend, and the Latin-influenced food and music scene is accessible without stretching.

housing.description: Quality 1BR in Brickell, Edgewater, or Coral Gables (Brickell 1BR ~$3,084; Edgewater ~$2,850; Coral Gables ~$2,930)

dining.description: Regular mid-range and fine dining in one of the country's best food cities

healthcare.description: Unsubsidized Miami-Dade Silver at full price (above the cliff); Miami-Dade carries among the nation's higher ACA benchmarks (avg Silver ~$1,125 age 50; FLOIR/MoneyGeek-derived)

transportation.description: Late-model car + premium Miami insurance + rideshare/parking; car-dependent

entertainment.description: Frequent nightlife/events, boating day trips on Biscayne Bay

3M.lifestyle: A quality one-bedroom in Brickell, Edgewater, or Coral Gables puts daily life in Miami's most desirable, walkable core, within reach of the water. Dining out lands several times a week across one of the country's most dynamic food scenes, and healthcare is now a full-price, unsubsidized plan — the heaviest recurring line after housing, because Florida carries among the highest ACA premiums in the nation and a FIRE income sits above the subsidy cliff. A late-model car with premium Miami insurance covers a car-dependent city, with boating day trips on Biscayne Bay and weekend drives to the Keys built in. Art Basel events, a Heat game, and a good gym all fit comfortably. At this level Miami is genuinely affluent, with the zero-income-tax advantage compounding at every turn.

housing.description: Luxury water-view 1BR/2BR in Brickell, Coral Gables, or Coconut Grove

dining.description: Frequent fine dining at the city's best rooms

healthcare.description: Rich unsubsidized Gold/PPO plus a direct-primary-care / concierge retainer

transportation.description: Luxury vehicle with Brickell parking, car service, boat slip on the bay

entertainment.description: Courtside Heat tickets, VIP nightlife, country-club access

luxuryExtras.description: Travel, wellness, club membership, personal training

5M.lifestyle: A luxury water-view apartment in Brickell, Coral Gables, or Coconut Grove, with a housekeeper on a weekly rhythm, marks a clearly upper-affluent Miami life. Fine dining is a frequent habit at the city's best rooms, healthcare adds a direct-primary-care or concierge retainer on top of a rich unsubsidized plan, and transport means a luxury vehicle with Brickell parking, car service, and a boat slip on the bay. Courtside Heat tickets, VIP nightlife, country-club access, and business-class travel to the Caribbean and Latin America all fit comfortably. Florida's zero income tax adds meaningful value at this spending level, sending the full withdrawal toward lifestyle rather than state taxes.

housing.description: Waterfront luxury condo, high-floor, in Brickell, on Key Biscayne, or on Fisher/Star Island

dining.description: Near-daily fine dining at the city's marquee tables

healthcare.description: Top-tier mainland PPO (unsubsidized) plus a concierge-medicine retainer (US-market basis, not a worldwide-expat plan)

transportation.description: Luxury car(s), car service, boat slip and upkeep

entertainment.description: VIP Art Basel, courtside seats, charters, events

domesticHelp.description: Near-daily housekeeper plus part-time personal assistant (staff-for-one)

luxuryExtras.description: First-class travel, yacht charter, luxury shopping, memberships, philanthropy

10M.lifestyle: A high-floor waterfront residence in Brickell or on Key Biscayne or Fisher Island, kept by near-daily household staff, sits at the top of what Miami money buys — second in this batch only to what New York commands. Dining is a near-daily affair at the city's marquee tables, healthcare pairs a top-tier mainland PPO with a concierge-medicine retainer, and transport spans a luxury vehicle, car service, and a slip on Biscayne Bay. VIP Art Basel access, courtside seats, yacht days to the Bahamas, and first-class travel are simply part of the calendar, with a generous discretionary and philanthropy budget on top. The glamour, the international energy, and the year-round warmth make this an uncapped luxury life — and Florida's zero state income tax keeps the entire withdrawal working toward it.
